statement: In Texas you change your legal name by filing a petition to change the name of an adult in the district court of the county where you live, and a judge signs an order granting it.
detail: Texas requires a set of fingerprints and a criminal-history (background) check as part of an adult name-change petition. The signed order is then used to update other documents.

cost.note: Filing fees vary by county; a fee waiver (Statement of Inability to Afford Payment) is available, and the fingerprint/background check may add a cost.

timeline.typical: several weeks, partly driven by the background check

statement: To change the name on your Texas driver's license or ID, visit the Department of Public Safety within the required time after your name change, bring your court order and proof of identity, and apply for a corrected card.

topic: Texas driver's license sex marker policy
statement: Texas's policy on changing the sex marker on a driver's license has changed recently and is contested.
detail: Because this is volatile, the navigator does not present a current rule here; it must be reverified against the official Department of Public Safety source before being shown as fact.
